concept.name: Expiration date
concept.definition: The date on which an option contract automatically expires and ceases to exist; it is the last day on which the option may be exercised (and for American-style options, the end of the exercise window).
concept.intuition: An option is a wasting asset with a printed shelf life: after the expiration date the contract is gone, worth whatever final settlement paid — usually zero for out-of-the-money options.
concept.mechanics: At expiration, in-the-money options are typically exercised 'by exception' above small thresholds (OCC uses $0.01 for equity options) unless contrary instructions are given, while out-of-the-money options expire worthless. Time value decays toward zero as expiration approaches, and for standard monthly U.S. equity options expiration falls on the third Friday of the expiration month.
concept.failure_modes: Traders who treat expiration day like any other trading day face pin risk (underlying closing near the strike), after-hours price moves that flip moneyness after the close, and automatic-exercise outcomes they did not intend.
concept.misconceptions: Expiration date is not always the last trading day: for many European-style index options the last trading day is the Thursday before expiration Friday, and the exercise style is set in each product's specifications.
concept.example: A standard U.S. equity option expiring in July ceases to exist after the third Friday of July; a holder who does not sell or exercise it by then keeps only any automatic-exercise value.
